notes: Grab (moto or car) is cheap; a scooter costs 150,000 VND a day (an international licence is required). Hoi An is 45 minutes away; the airport is inside the city.

From October to January expect rain and floods (Hoi An can go under water), with temperatures of 20-25°C. February to May is ideal (dry, 28°C). The Hoi An lantern festival takes place every month at full moon.
The Vietnam e-visa is valid for 90 days (e-visa for Turkish citizens). Use cash in VND (1 USD ≈ 25,000, ASSUMPTION); cards are only accepted in hotels.
Bánh mì costs 25,000-30,000 VND, mì quảng 40,000, a restaurant meal 150,000-250,000, Ba Na 950,000 and the Hoi An ticket 120,000. There is no tipping; haggle at markets.
Get to Ba Na at the 08:00 opening (the Golden Bridge is empty) and Mỹ Sơn at 07:00. Visit the Marble Mountains in the morning; the Dragon Bridge show is on Saturdays and Sundays at 21:00.
Try cao lầu (Hoi An), mì quảng, bánh xèo, salt coffee and egg coffee. Street food is safe; pick a busy stall.

stops.name: My Khe Beach
stops.tips: In winter (October to January) the sea is rough and rainy, so stick to a walk along the beach.

stops.name: Bánh Mì Bà Lan
stops.tips: Da Nang's legendary bánh mì (Vietnamese baguette sandwich). Expect a queue in the morning.

stops.name: Linh Ung Pagoda Lady Buddha
stops.tips: A 67 m Lady Buddha on the Son Tra Peninsula with views over the bay. 20 minutes by scooter or Grab.

stops.name: Mì Quảng 1A
stops.tips: The classic Quang noodle dish (mì quảng), on Hai Phong Street.

stops.name: Dragon Bridge Fire Show
stops.tips: On Saturdays and Sundays at 21:00 the dragon breathes fire and water. One of the Han River bridges.

backups.name: Han Market
backups.tips: The central market, with a food floor and dried fruit.

backups.name: Museum of Cham Sculpture
backups.tips: The world's largest collection of Cham sculpture. On a rainy day, come here instead of the Buddha.

stops.name: Ba Na Hills Cable Car
stops.tips: One of the world's longest cable cars (5.8 km), climbing to 1,487 m. The all-day ticket is 950,000 VND; it opens at 08:00.

stops.name: Golden Bridge Cầu Vàng
stops.tips: A golden bridge held up by giant stone hands. It gets crowded after 09:30 and fog can roll in.

stops.name: Le Jardin d'Amour & Linh Ung Ba Na
stops.tips: French-style gardens and a pagoda at the top.

stops.name: French Village Ba Na
stops.tips: A replica French village and Fantasy Park (including an indoor amusement park), with shows.

stops.name: Ba Na Buffet Lunch
stops.tips: There are buffet restaurants at the top. Head back down at 15:00.

backups.name: Fantasy Park Ba Na
backups.tips: The indoor amusement park is included in the ticket. If you are travelling with children, come here instead of the village.

backups.name: Bếp Cuốn Da Nang
backups.tips: An evening meal in the city: Vietnamese rolls (cuốn) with platters to wrap your own.

stops.name: Marble Mountains Ngũ Hành Sơn
stops.tips: Five marble hills, with a beam of light in Huyen Khong Cave. The lift costs 15,000 VND; mornings are cooler.

stops.name: Hội An Ancient Town
stops.tips: A UNESCO-listed port town from the 16th century, with yellow houses and the Japanese Bridge. A five-site ticket costs 120,000 VND.

stops.name: Bánh Mì Phượng
stops.tips: Bourdain's bánh mì, in Hoi An.

stops.name: Hội An Bebe Tailor
stops.tips: A made-to-measure suit in 24 hours. Hoi An has more than 400 tailors.

stops.name: Hội An Lantern Night & Thu Bồn Boat
stops.tips: A lantern boat on the river costs 150,000 VND. There is a festival at full moon, plus the Nguyen Hoang night market. Try cao lầu (Hoi An noodles) at dinner.

backups.name: Morning Glory Hoi An
backups.tips: Ms Vy's restaurant, serving cao lầu and white rose dumplings.

backups.name: Precious Heritage Museum Réhahn
backups.tips: The photographer's portraits of 54 ethnic groups, free entry. Come here instead of the tailor.

days.theme: Hải Vân Pass and Lăng Cô

stops.name: Hải Vân Pass
stops.tips: Top Gear's "best coastal road in the world". Ride up by scooter, with an easy rider tour, or go by car. The pass rises to 500 m and has French and US bunkers.

stops.name: Lăng Cô Lagoon
stops.tips: A turquoise lagoon and fishing village, with oyster farms.

stops.name: Lăng Cô Seafood Restaurant
stops.tips: A wooden restaurant over the lagoon, serving oysters and prawns.

stops.name: Elephant Springs Suối Voi
stops.tips: It is cold in winter. Walk along Lăng Cô beach and look out for the view of Bach Ma.

stops.name: Nam Ô Reef Sunset
stops.tips: A rocky headland on the way back to Da Nang, with seaweed-covered rocks (green in March and April).

backups.name: Bạch Mã National Park
backups.tips: Cloud forest and ruined French villas, with jeep tours. Come here instead of the springs.

backups.name: Bé Mặn Nam Ô
backups.tips: Grilled fish by the sea, in Nam Ô.

stops.name: Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary
stops.tips: Hindu temples of the Champa Kingdom from the 4th to 13th centuries (a cousin of Angkor). It is empty when it opens at 07:00. The Apsara dance is at 09:30 and the tour takes 1.5 hours.

stops.name: Mỹ Sơn Village Restaurant
stops.tips: A village breakfast or lunch, with bánh xèo (crispy savoury pancakes).

stops.name: Thanh Hà Pottery Village
stops.tips: A 500-year-old pottery village near Hoi An. Try the potter's wheel and see Terracotta Park.

stops.name: An Bàng Beach
stops.tips: Rough in winter. Beach bars and a walk along the sand.

stops.name: Sound of Silence An Bang
stops.tips: A beach cafe for coffee at sunset.

backups.name: Trà Quế Vegetable Village
backups.tips: An organic garden village with cycling and cooking classes. Come here instead of the pottery village.

stops.name: Cù Lao Chàm Island Speedboat
stops.tips: The sea is closed in winter, so take a day trip to Hue (2.5 hours). Visit the Imperial City and Tu Duc Tomb; the Imperial City ticket is 200,000 VND.

stops.name: Cù Lao Chàm Snorkelling
stops.tips: In Hue, visit Thien Mu Pagoda and take a boat on the Perfume River.

stops.name: Island Fishing Village Lunch
stops.tips: In Hue, try Bún Bò Huế Mệ Kéo for Hue noodle soup.

stops.name: Da Nang Evening at Bà Dưỡng Bánh Xèo
stops.tips: Da Nang's crispy pancakes (bánh xèo) and nem lụi (lemongrass skewers), in a Hoàng Diệu side street.

backups.name: Hue Imperial City
backups.tips: The Purple Forbidden City. Go in winter or if the sea is closed.

backups.name: Quán Trần Da Nang
backups.tips: Bánh tráng cuốn thịt heo (pork rice-paper rolls), a local favourite.

stops.name: Cà Phê Muối Salt Coffee
stops.tips: Hue-style coffee with salted foam, best in the morning.

stops.name: Con Market Chợ Cồn
stops.tips: A local market for dried beef (bò khô) and coffee to take home.

stops.name: Han River Promenade
stops.tips: A riverside walk past the Love Lock Bridge and the Golden Dragon.

stops.name: Madame Lân
stops.tips: A wide Vietnamese menu on the riverbank. Have bún chả cá for your farewell meal.

stops.name: Da Nang Airport
stops.tips: 10 minutes from the city by Grab. Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Bún Chả Cá 109
backups.tips: Fish cake noodle soup, on Nguyễn Chí Thanh Street.

backups.name: Da Nang Museum
backups.tips: The city's history. Come here instead of the market.
